correctness.rationale: Two standalone scripts independently build isomorphic Fano incidence graphs by respectively the cyclic (7,3,1) difference set and nonzero GF(2)^3 incidence. Exact closed-neighborhood domination and every subset of the 14-vertex graph were checked, recovering all 65 inclusion-minimal sets and verifying the four geometric families exactly. Each k-budget graph was explicitly generated by single-bit toggles. All 5 component multisets and edge counts agreed across Python and C++. Every source vertex of each main component had a full BFS from which exact radius and diameter were attained: (1,2),(10,12),(11,14),(12,14) at k=5,6,7,8. The all-graphs minimal-set-overlap equivalence is independently proved in RESULT.md. No larger-graph inference is made from this finite test.

value.rationale: Heawood is the canonical smallest nontrivial projective-plane incidence graph. Minimal dominating configurations form geometrically natural point-line families, and budgets 4–8 are forced by the minimum and upper domination numbers, rather than chosen for numerology. Their distinct isolation transitions form an exact natural classification of a state graph, while sharp eccentricities answer the type of metric question explicitly posed by the founding TAR paper. The new exact distances and component orders are not deductions of generic connectivity theorems or an ordinary domination polynomial and offer a useful finite benchmark for projective-incidence reconfiguration.
